taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: Agent broker downstream account selection and token-exchange delegation
controls.source_trace: Determine whether a tool request can select a different user/account/resource while the broker reuses a more privileged downstream token.
controls.implementation_branch: Map the broker client, consenting user, downstream resource and requested scopes into the token used by the tool. Consent to one service/tenant does not automatically authorize another. A broad token may be intentional but still needs per-user tool-action checks; inspect token exchange and audience binding without using real delegated tokens against unrelated services.
controls.operational_method: Specialize in broker account selection and token exchange: initiating client/user, selected downstream connection, resource/audience, scopes and any actor/subject chain. Compare two owned connection handles for the same provider and a changed account after consent. A broker must apply the actual per-client consent/action policy before selecting the token; merely returning a correctly signed token for the wrong stored connection can violate authority without any token forgery.
controls.controlled_verification: Use two owned provider connection handles and one broker client consent, then switch the selected account/resource or actor chain before an inert downstream consumer. Compare exact consent-preserving selection with the prohibited connection.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: An authenticated broker or broad token in its vault is not a bypass if every tool operation correctly constrains the caller.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Bind tool caller, consented resource and downstream action, testing revocation and authorized multi-account use.
